method: brute force over all linear orders for every DAG on n topologically ordered nodes

minimal_counterexample.why: Desc+(A)={A,D}, Desc+(B)={B,D}, Desc+(C)={C,D} all must be intervals, so D would need three distinct adjacent positions in a linear order

interpretation: a prefix/interval encoding is exact only for the forest case and for DAGs that admit a consecutive-ones order
the real DAG has 310 concepts with >=3 parents, so a single trie cannot represent it without duplication or loss
limits: enumerates DAGs that respect one fixed topological order; relabelling is irrelevant since intervalizability depends only on the edge set
no heuristic run on the 1,929-concept DAG; the parent count is a necessary-condition signal, not a proof of failure
